subject.title: Chronic agent failures on Telegram — LLM timeouts before configured timeout + silent incomplete turns + dead fallbacks (OpenRouter/DeepSeek+V4-Flash, v2026.5.28)

question: Is current source and latest-release component coverage enough to close #88907, or should maintainers first run a Telegram/OpenRouter live repro and split any remaining failure by layer?
rationale: The codebase now contains targeted fixes for several named symptoms, but the issue combines provider timeout, fallback, incomplete-turn, and Telegram delivery behavior that cannot be safely resolved from source inspection alone.

options.title: Run live repro then split
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer correlates current-main/latest-release behavior with sanitized config and runId logs, then closes fixed subpaths or creates one narrow remaining issue.

options.title: Close as covered by component fixes
options.body: Close now based on current source and related closed issues, accepting the risk that the reporter's exact Telegram/OpenRouter setup was not revalidated.

options.title: Keep as broad tracker
options.body: Leave the composite report open as-is without narrowing, which preserves context but makes any future automated repair poorly targeted.

recommendation.title: Run live repro then split
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer correlates current-main/latest-release behavior with sanitized config and runId logs, then closes fixed subpaths or creates one narrow remaining issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this owner to the largest set of current timeout, failover, and reply-delivery paths involved in the proof decision.
